topic.angle: Why some Roman harbours and buildings are still standing after two thousand years

body.question: Roman harbour concrete has outlasted much modern concrete. What helps it survive seawater?
options: Seawater reacts with its volcanic ash and lime to form rare crystals
It is made with iron bars
The Romans sealed it with wax
body.reveal: The strength and longevity of Roman marine concrete is understood to benefit from a reaction of seawater with volcanic ash and quicklime. It creates a rare crystal called tobermorite, which may resist fracturing. Research in 2023 also found that lime clasts could help the concrete self-repair cracks.
